findings.explanation: The flagged sink is `session.execute(text("SELECT id, username, role FROM users WHERE " + where), params)`. The only dynamic part of the SQL string is `where`, which is built from `clauses` where each clause is `f"{field} = :{field}"`. The `field` value is strictly validated against the hard-coded allowlist `ALLOWED_FILTER_FIELDS = {"username", "role", "email"}` and any field not in the set returns a 400 before reaching the query. The user-controlled `value` is never interpolated into the SQL string; it is passed as a bound parameter via `params[field] = value` and referenced by the named placeholder `:{field}`. This matches the project's security policy (security-policy.md §5) which requires bound parameters and allowlist validation of dynamic identifiers. The `text()` + named-parameter pattern with a separate params dict is the exact parameterization the policy mandates, so no user-controlled input can alter the query structure or inject SQL.

evidence.content: All SQL statements MUST use bound parameters (SQLAlchemy `text()` with `:name` parameters, or DB-API placeholders with a separate params argument). String interpolation, f-strings, `%` formatting, `.format()`, or string concatenation of request-derived values into SQL is forbidden (CWE-89). Dynamic identifiers (table or column names, sort keys) MUST be validated against a hard-coded allowlist before being placed in a query.

findings.explanation: The new GET /users/filter endpoint is a user-listing operation. The security policy (security-policy.md §2) states 'Listing all users (GET /users) requires the manager role or above,' and api-spec.md lists user-listing/search endpoints (/users, /users/search) as 'manager, admin'. The changed code enforces this with @require_role("manager") (app/routes/users.py, new filter_users), which is the exact decorator mandated by policy §1 ('Endpoints MUST use the decorators provided in app/auth.py'). The require_role decorator (app/auth.py:69-85) correctly authenticates via bearer token and enforces ROLE_RANK (user<manager<admin), so managers and admins pass while plain users get 403. This matches the documented access rule for user-listing endpoints, so the authorization is correct. (Note: the SQL construction is parameterized and field-allowlisted, so it is not an authorization flaw; the SAST SQLi heuristic is a false positive for this authz review.)

evidence.content: Listing all users (`GET /users`) requires the **manager** role or above.
| `/users` | GET | manager, admin | ... | `/users/search` | GET | manager, admin |
Endpoints MUST use the decorators provided in `app/auth.py` (`@require_auth`, `@require_role`, `@require_api_key_scope`).
